speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with sudden-onset vertigo; to begin our evaluation, have you experienced any hearing loss, tinnitus, or a feeling of fullness in your ear alongside the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient describes a brief episode of spontaneous vertigo lasting three minutes with no hearing loss or tinnitus. To narrow the differential, have you experienced any severe headache, double vision, difficulty speaking, or weakness in your arms or legs during or after the episode?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: No neurological deficits such as weakness, speech difficulties, or vision changes were noted, and you are currently at baseline. Given the brief duration of your vertigo and lack of focal signs, have you noticed any recent severe neck pain or heard a loud "pop" in your neck prior to the episode?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The clinical picture of spontaneous vertigo lasting only three minutes without hearing loss, neurological deficits, or neck trauma is classic for BPPV. While your history of eczema is noted, it is not a contributing factor to this condition.
